summary: US-O2b: A refund gives the capacity back
description:
**As** an organizer, **I want** a refunded ticket's seat to go back on sale, **so that** the capacity a refund frees can actually be resold.

**Priority:** P0  **Depends on:** TKT-157 (tickets are voided first)

**Created at TKT-157's planning (2026-07-31)** — the capacity-return half of the original TKT-157. See TKT-157's `kind=plan-final` for why the split runs by reversal rather than by service, and why voiding goes first: freeing capacity while the original ticket still admits is the one ordering that can oversell.

The plan draft's **Q1** answers this ticket's design and is inherited verbatim: `claims.returned_quantity` orthogonal to `claims.status`, with `claim_history` (`action='refund_return'`, `idempotency_key='refund:'||refund_id`) as the durable idempotency receipt, inside inventory's pool-lock-first claim transaction.

**It also inherits the draft's seated finding, which is the hard part:** *no persistent mapping connects an access ticket to a `claim_seats.seat_identity`*, so a partial return of a seated claim has no correct semantics. Support full seated returns (release every seat) and refuse partial ones **before money moves**; record the limitation in ADR-038 rather than hiding it behind a successful quantity update.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A supported return decrements `inventory_pools.confirmed_quantity` and the claim's unreturned quantity by exactly q under the pool lock. **AC amended from the original TKT-157 wording** (accepted at TKT-157 planning): “availability increases by exactly q” holds literally only for an open pool with no draining capacity cut and no channel masking. The universal invariant is: *remaining confirmed demand decreases by exactly q, once; availability stays within `[0, effective capacity]`; in an ordinary open GA pool public availability increases by exactly q.*
- [ ] Replaying the same refund identity returns a replay answer, writes no second `claim_history` row, and leaves the counters unchanged.
- [ ] The return runs inside inventory's row-locked claim transaction (ADR-010). A contention test proves `confirmed_quantity >= 0`, `returned_quantity <= quantity`, and one refund identity applied once.
- [ ] Every channel-consumption aggregate subtracts `returned_quantity` from confirmed claims, so returned capacity is not double-counted as still sold.
- [ ] A **full** seated return releases every live `claim_seats` row in the same transaction; a **partial** seated return is refused before any money moves.
- [ ] Capacity returned is visible on the refund (`order_refunds.capacity_returned_at`) and retryable by replaying the refund idempotency key.
- [ ] Spec declared, generated code committed, smoke coverage (ADR-009/028/030).

Quality gates: `make check` green; contract tests; `organizer_id`-scoped entities; money untouched (this ticket moves no money).

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code — floats are banned on money paths.

Traceability is a must, for money and tickets: money-relevant records land as immutable, hash-chained, signed journal entries from the first order (corrections = compensating entries; read models = projections), and every ticket/entitlement state change (issued, delivered, transferred, resold, exchanged, redeemed, reissued, invalidated) is an append-only lifecycle event linked to its order.

governingAdrs.why: Every lifecycle event goes through store.appendLifecycle — the verifier asserts one-to-one coverage, so a direct INSERT into lifecycle_events reads as tampering and fails `access verify-lifecycle` in the gate. Canonical forms are pinned by golden literals; changing a byte is a canonical-version migration, not a test update. Also: name the adversary before writing 'tamper-evident'.

Inventory's claim transaction is the contention path. Giving capacity back must go through the same row-locked transaction discipline; a plain UPDATE outside it can drive confirmed_quantity negative or double-return under concurrency.
Capacity adjustments clamp rather than reject. Returning capacity must not let availability exceed the pool's capacity, and the clamp reasoning is the precedent for what to do when it would.

Corrections are COMPENSATING ENTRIES, never mutations. A refund/exchange appends a new signed fact; the original sale fact and its hash link are untouched. The payments journal has a DB trigger that raises on UPDATE/DELETE — any design that 'adjusts' a fact is rejected by the database, not by review.

If any domain event payload changes or a new one is published: bump on CONSUMER SEMANTICS, not parse compatibility, and consumers dispatch on `schema` BEFORE decoding `data`. A fixture built from the type under test cannot fail.

Fail closed. Responses are validated against the spec; an undeclared status code becomes a 500. Every new endpoint must declare every status it can answer, and a downstream answer commerce cannot validate aborts rather than degrades.

Contract-first. A new operation is written in the service's openapi.yaml first, then `openapi_gen.go` / `api-types.gen.ts` are regenerated and COMMITTED before the gate runs — check-generate diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift.
Commerce and inventory ARE inside the smoke happy-path coverage gate. A new documented 2xx operation must be exercised through the running stack or the suite fails.

Migrations run out-of-band via each binary's `migrate` subcommand as a one-shot Compose job. Add the SQL under the service's internal/store/migrations/ with the next number; the server path never migrates.

objective.note: Without it a refund frees no capacity and the organizer cannot resell the seat — the second half of TKT-9's first COS.

scope.note: IN: inventory partial/full return, channel aggregates, seated full-return + partial refusal, the commerce leg that drives it. OUT: ticket voiding (TKT-157), exchange (TKT-158), bulk cancellation (TKT-159), persistent ticket-to-seat identity (needs its own ticket).

uncertainties.note: Whether the pre-money seated-eligibility check is a new inventory read operation or a field on an existing one is a Planning-time call; both are reversible.

dependencies.note: blocked-by TKT-157. Everything else exists on main.

approach.note: Inherited verbatim from TKT-157's plan draft Q1 — see that ticket's kind=plan comment, which this ticket's implementer should read before drafting its own.

first_slice.note: GA partial return, proven end to end: refund, availability rises by exactly q, replay moves nothing.

success.note: Demoable: refund 1 of 2, watch availability rise by 1, replay and watch it not move again.

context_memo.note: Inherited from TKT-157 (ADR-037 and ADR-031 included, both added at TKT-157's claim). Re-validate at claim: ADR-038 will exist by then.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### ✅ Implementation readiness — PASS

Born from TKT-157's planning split, not from shaping — so this is a verdict on inherited work, and the inheritance is the point: the design (Q1), the seated finding, and the amended availability AC all come from a cross-model-reviewed plan rather than being re-derived here. The context-mémo is inherited whole.

**Concerns:** none blocking. One to carry: **re-validate the mémo at claim.** ADR-038 will exist by then (TKT-157 writes it) and will govern this ticket directly — the same staleness that bit TKT-157, whose bake-time mémo was missing ADR-037 and ADR-031.

**Verdict:** PASS.
